\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Daily returns of the straddle position over the out-of-sample period, \rheSampleStart{} to
\rheSampleEnd{} ($T_{\mathrm{oos}} = \rheNdays$ trading days). The sign strategy holds
$q_t = \sign(\hat\sigma^2_t - \mathrm{IV}^2_t)$ straddles; the short-straddle benchmark (Short straddle) holds
$q_t \equiv -1$; every model except the
OLS uses the full predictor set. Mean return is at mid-quotes, in percent of the premium; $\SR$ is the annualized
Sharpe ratio at mid-quotes and at quoted bid/ask prices; hit rate and long days are the shares of days with
$r_t > 0$ at mid-quotes and with $q_t = +1$. $\Delta\SR$ is $\SR$ at mid-quotes minus that of the short-straddle
benchmark (\rheShortSh); in parentheses, the $t$-statistic of the mean return (Newey--West with bandwidth $S = \rheHACS$ and fixed-$b$ critical values, \citealp{LazarusLewisStockWatson2018}; Section~\ref{sec:rh_methods_tests}); under $\Delta\SR$, the $p$-value of the \citet{LedoitWolf2008} bootstrap test of equal Sharpe ratios on the \rheSzDays{} post-warmup days, in brackets (Section~\ref{sec:rh_methods_tests}).
$^{*}$, $^{**}$ and $^{***}$ denote significance at the 10\%, 5\% and 1\% levels.
Panel A: models estimated on the 30-minute intervals of the day (the pooled intraday scheme; the tree ensembles on
the \rheTreeNBars{} regular-hours intervals, note a); Panel B: models
estimated on the closing interval only (one observation a day). Every model row trades the forecast of the 15:30--16:00 ET
variance made at 15:30.
\item[a] Pooled intraday tree ensembles, fitted on the design of the pooled linear models of Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos}:
the \rheTreeNBars{} regular-hours 30-minute intervals of each day, re-estimated at every interval on a rolling window
of \rheTreeWindowDays{} trading days ($W = \rheTreeWindowBars$ intervals); hyperparameters from an Optuna search, one
configuration per method, not re-tuned (Appendix~\ref{sec:rh_exp_schemes}). No ex-post selection.
\end{tablenotes}
\end{threeparttable}
